To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a four amino acid signal is necessary and sufficient to target a vacuolar protein to the vacuolar membrane, and that mutations in the vacuolar signal are cis-dominantly misdirected.
the amino acid sequence of the vacuole targeting signal of proCPY was identified by site-directed mutagenesis, and that the sorting defect of mutant proCPYs is cis-dominant.
the vacuolar sorting information in the propeptide of CPY is contained within a short stretch of amino acids that are essential for the targeting process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the intracellular sorting of proteins in yeast.
the mechanism of vacuolar protein sorting in Saccharomyces.
the mechanism of vacuolar targeting of the vacuole hydrolases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vacuolar sorting signal of CPY is the four-amino-acid sequence Gln-Arg- Pro-Leu.
the four amino acids, GPRL, are necessary and sufficient for the vacuolar sorting of proCPY.
the PRC signal is defined by 4 amino acid residues, GPRR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the vacuolar sorting information in proCPY is contained in a 16 residue sequence and that this sequence is recognized by a sorting apparatus that functions independently of the secretory apparatus and the cytoplasmic membrane.
the PRCI missorting mutation results in a failure of proCPY to interact with a sorting apparatus, which is composed of a receptor and an adaptor protein.
the vacuolar sorting signal of proCPY is composed of four amino acids and is not a secondary structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vacuolar sorting machinery of the yeast cell is very robust.
the four amino acids of the vacuole targeting signal (VTS) are the minimal requirements for sorting.
a small number of contiguous amino acids can define a targeting signal.
